$comment: Third-party repositories this fork adapts files from, without being a fork of them.
Check them: node --experimental-strip-types .claude/scripts/upstream-check.ts (run from the repo root; --help for options).
pinned = the upstream commit the adaptations were written from, as cited in the license file.
reviewed = the last upstream commit someone checked the adaptations against; the check reports what changed since.
adaptations = each local file and the upstream files it adapts. A change there needs a human look.
context = upstream files the adaptations lean on without copying them. A change there is worth a glance.
watch_new = upstream globs where a new file may be worth adapting too.
After a review, --record moves reviewed to the upstream head. Moving pinned is a separate decision: it means the adaptations were brought in line, and the license file's commit moves with it.

reviewed.note: v0.20.0 plus Unreleased (7f4ddfd). Nothing adapted: the adapted commands changed only by an author-credit footer (the fork's Adapts headers and .claude/licenses/obsidian-second-brain.md already carry the credit and the MIT notice; the footer's contact and consulting links are not license terms), checkin.py by an SPDX header, research.md by an opt-in Keenable web source (om-research queries scholarly databases only). Context: SKILL.md drops the curl-to-shell bootstrap; ai-first-rules.md makes a speculation source a proposal at compile time, which every om-* write already is, since nothing is written without approval.

v1.0.0 (d60674f). Adapted: verified records only a check other than compilation (a /om-wiki-lint --deep pass the user approved, or the user's own check), so om-wiki-compile and om-wiki-thesis no longer set it, lint accepts its absence and lists never-verified pages, and the Wiki base shows them under Check due; lint reports footnote references without a definition and unused definitions. pinned moved to this head with it. Not adapted: the five-point confidence (the fork's three levels each have a source criterion, the two new ones have none), raw namespaces and --raw-subdir (wiki/raw/ is flat by design), manifest-only Git ingestion, the owner fix for raw pointers (raw notes hold their content), the C20 engine and identity checks (no hub), the ambiguous wikilink check (the vault-wide link test owns resolution), the refresh workflow (raw is already create-only, a newer version is a new file).

Head of main (d9bae99). Adapted: the outline agent's two-level search plan, the literature-review rater's caps, the side-by-side comparison in both orders. Not adapted: the citation quota, the refinement prompt's rule never to state a limitation, the 'gain covers drop' acceptance rule, plotting, LaTeX templates and the PDF formatting review. Watched for later: P0/P1 citation priorities (citation_f1.py) and fuzzy title matching against a database (scholar_utils.py).
